name: RFID reader (RC522) and tags
author: Bench Workshop
description: The RC522 RFID reader (SPI) with MIFARE Classic tags: a white card and a blue key fob. Hold a tag up to the reader (drag it within a few cm of the coil) and the program reads its ID, and can read and write its 1 KB memory. Includes MFRC522.h.

parts.name: RFID reader (RC522)
parts.description: SPI: SDA is its chip select (to any pin), SCK, MOSI, MISO to the board's SPI pins, RST to a pin, 3.3V (not 5 V!), GND. It reads a tag held within about 4 cm of its coil. #include <SPI.h> and <MFRC522.h>; MFRC522 rfid(SS_PIN, RST_PIN); SPI.begin(); rfid.PCD_Init(); then rfid.PICC_IsNewCardPresent() && rfid.PICC_ReadCardSerial(): rfid.uid.uidByte[0..3]. The run panel can hold up a tag too.

parts.name: RFID card (MIFARE 1K)
parts.description: A white card with a chip and a coil. Drag it onto the reader's coil to read it. Each card has its own 4-byte ID (set it below, as hex).

parts.name: RFID key fob (MIFARE 1K)
parts.description: A blue key fob: the same chip as the card, in a little case. Drag it onto the reader's coil.

examples.name: Door lock
examples.description: Drag the key fob onto the reader: the green LED says it's let in. The white card isn't on the list: red. Its serial monitor shows each tag's ID and counts its visits in the tag's own memory (block 4).
